author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: An AI code editor that writes and edits software alongside the programmer.
what_it_does: Cursor, built by Anysphere, is a code editor with AI woven through it. Developers describe what they want and it writes or changes the code. It reached significant revenue faster than almost any software company on record.
how_it_makes_money: Monthly subscriptions per developer, with higher tiers for heavier use and team plans for companies.
why_it_matters: It is the fastest revenue ramp in this coverage and the clearest evidence that AI coding tools convert to paid usage rather than staying a demo.
competitive_position: Competes with GitHub Copilot, which has Microsoft's distribution, and with tools from the model labs themselves, several of which supply the models Cursor runs on.
key_risks: It depends on models made by companies that also sell competing products.
Model costs scale directly with usage, squeezing margin as customers use it more.
Switching editors is easy, so retention is less certain than in enterprise software.
A model provider could bundle equivalent capability into its own subscription.

glossary.definition: Integrated development environment: the application programmers write code in.
What is left from a sale after the direct cost of delivering it. For AI products the model cost is the main deduction.
